text: Welcome to today's mechanical keyboard build session in the workshop! I'm Sarah, and I'll be putting together this custom 65% keyboard that was designed by my colleague Marcus last month. First, let me set up the workbench with all the premium tools and components that we'll need for this build. The high-quality PCB with hot-swap sockets and pre-installed SMD components was manufactured by our supplier three weeks ago using advanced pick-and-place machinery. Now, I'm going to heat up my soldering iron to exactly 315 degrees Celsius while Marcus takes apart the packaging and organizes the Gateron Yellow switches. The custom aluminum case that Marcus ordered from the CNC shop has been anodized to a beautiful space gray finish. Next, I'll hook up the PCB tester to verify all connections are working properly before we move forward. The foam padding and plate foam, which were cut to precise 2.5 millimeter thickness specifications, need to be installed first. After that, Marcus and I will work together to install all 68 switches into the hot-swap sockets. The stabilizers that came with this kit were pre-lubricated by the manufacturer using Krytox 205g0, but we're going to tune them up with our own application. While I'm applying the lubricant with a size 00 brush, Marcus is carefully installing the spacebar stabilizer wire that measures exactly 7 units or 133 millimeters in length. The keycaps that we'll be using are double-shot PBT caps in the Cherry profile, and they were produced by a factory in Taiwan. Finally, after all components are assembled and the firmware is flashed, the completed keyboard will be tested using our switch tester and typing software for about 5 minutes to ensure everything works perfectly.
